title: The Roles & Permissions list page loads with its columns and a create button
custom_preconds: 1. You are logged in as an admin on Settings > Roles & Permissions.
custom_steps:
1. Open Settings > Roles & Permissions.
  2. Look at the page heading, the table columns and the create button.
custom_expected:
The page heading reads Roles & Permissions.

The table shows columns for the role name, description, template, role type, users and an actions column (with a lock icon on system-role rows).

There is a button to create a new role.

(Confirm the exact column order and button label live.)

title: All 11 system roles appear in the list with a system badge
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the role name column for the system roles.
  2. Look at the type column for each row.
custom_expected:
All 11 system roles are listed: Administrator, Service Manager, Senior Service Advisor, Service Advisor, Foreman, Technician, Parts Manager, Parts Technician, Office User, Sales Representative, Time Clock User.

Each is marked as a system role.

There is no Owner role (it is merged into Administrator).

title: A custom role row has a pencil (edit) icon and a three-dot menu; View Permissions is in the menu
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list with at least one custom role.
custom_steps:
1. Find a custom role row.
  2. Look at the icons in the Actions column.
custom_expected:
A custom role row has a pencil (edit) icon and a three-dot menu.

There is no separate eye icon on custom rows — View Permissions is inside the three-dot menu.

(A separate eye icon appears only on the locked system rows Office User and Time Clock User.)

title: The eye (View Permissions) icon shows in the Actions column only for Office User and Time Clock User
custom_preconds: 1. You are logged in as an admin on Settings > Roles & Permissions.
custom_steps:
1. Open Settings > Roles & Permissions.
  2. Look at the Actions column for the Office User and Time Clock User rows.
  3. Look at the Actions column for the other roles.
  4. On one other role, open the three-dot menu and look at the options.
custom_expected:
A standalone eye icon appears in the Actions column only for Office User and Time Clock User (the non-editable roles).

Every other role has no standalone eye icon; those rows reach View Permissions through the three-dot menu.

title: The Office User system role is non-editable (lock icon, eye only)
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Find the Office User row.
  2. Look at the role name column.
  3. Look at the Actions column.
  4. Click the eye icon.
custom_expected:
A lock icon shows next to Office User.

The Actions column has only the eye icon — no pencil, no three-dot menu.

The eye opens a read-only Permission Summary for Office User.

title: The Time Clock User system role is non-editable (lock icon, eye only)
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Find the Time Clock User row.
  2. Look at the role name column.
  3. Look at the Actions column.
  4. Click the eye icon.
custom_expected:
A lock icon shows next to Time Clock User.

The Actions column has only the eye icon.

The eye opens a read-only Permission Summary.

title: The Users column shows a clickable count that links to the filtered Staff page
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the Users column for a role that has one or more users.
  2. Click the count.
  3. Look at the Users column for a role with zero users.
custom_expected:
A non-zero count is a clickable link.

Clicking it opens the Staff page filtered to that role.

A zero count is shown as a non-clickable '0'.

title: The search field filters the roles list as you type
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Find the search field.
  2. Type a role name (for example Technician).
custom_expected: The list filters as you type, narrowing to matching roles.

title: Roles & Permissions is hidden for users without the App Settings sub-toggle
custom_preconds: 1. A user is assigned a role with Settings off, or Settings on but the App Settings sub-toggle off.
custom_steps:
1. Log in as that user.
  2. Look at the left sidebar.
custom_expected: Either the Settings area does not appear, or the Roles & Permissions item is not shown under it.

title: Locations appears under the Settings area
custom_preconds: 1. You are logged in with Settings access.
custom_steps:
1. Open the Settings area in the sidebar.
  2. List the items.
custom_expected: The Settings area includes Locations (alongside Settings, Staff, Roles & Permissions and Departments).

title: The roles list has a Template column
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the column headers.
  2. Look at the Template values for system-role rows.
  3. Look at the Template values for custom-role rows.
custom_expected:
There is a Template column.

A custom role shows the system template it was created from.

(Confirm the exact system-role Template value live.)

title: Each of the 11 system roles shows its description
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Count the system roles.
  2. Read each system role's Description.
custom_expected:
There are 11 system roles.

Each shows a description (for example Administrator = full system access; Service Manager = full operational access with limited admin; and so on).

(Confirm the exact description text live.)

title: A custom role with no description shows a dash
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list with a custom role that has no description.
custom_steps: 1. Look at the Description column for that role.
custom_expected: A dash '-' is shown when a custom role has no description.

title: An editable system role's three-dot menu shows View Permissions and no Delete
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Open the three-dot menu on an editable system role (for example Administrator or Service Manager).
  2. List the menu options.
custom_expected:
The menu has no Delete option (system roles cannot be deleted).

(Note: the build has a Duplicate Role feature — confirm live whether Duplicate appears in this menu; the older 'no Duplicate' expectation may be out of date.)

title: The three-dot menu is hidden on the non-editable system roles (Office User, Time Clock User)
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Find the Office User row and the Time Clock User row.
  2. Look at the Actions column for each.
custom_expected: Only the eye icon is shown for Office User and Time Clock User — no pencil and no three-dot menu.

title: A custom role's three-dot menu shows View Permissions and Delete
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list with a custom role that has 0 users.
custom_steps:
1. Open the three-dot menu on that custom role row.
  2. List the menu options.
custom_expected:
The menu shows View Permissions and Delete (Delete in red with a trash icon).

Edit is the separate pencil icon, not in the menu.

(Confirm live whether a Duplicate option also appears, since the build has a Duplicate Role feature.)

title: Deletion and duplication behavior on the roles list
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list with both system and custom roles.
custom_steps:
1. Open the three-dot menu on a system role.
  2. Open the three-dot menu on a custom role.
  3. Look for Delete and for a Duplicate option in each.
custom_expected:
System roles cannot be deleted (no Delete in their menu).

Custom roles with 0 users can be deleted.

The build has a Duplicate Role feature — confirm live where Duplicate appears; the older 'no Duplicate action exists anywhere' expectation may be out of date.

title: The template picker lists all 11 system role templates with descriptions
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Start creating a custom role.
  2. Count and read the template options.
custom_expected:
The template picker lists 11 templates, one per system role (Administrator, Service Manager, Senior Service Advisor, Service Advisor, Foreman, Technician, Parts Manager, Parts Technician, Office User, Sales Representative, Time Clock User), each with a short description.

(Exact modal title/labels to be confirmed live.)

title: Applying a template opens the Create Role page pre-filled with that template's settings
custom_preconds: 1. The template picker is open with the Service Advisor template selected.
custom_steps:
1. Apply the selected template.
  2. Look at the page that opens.
  3. Scroll to the permissions.
  4. Check the Work orders card boxes.
  5. Check the Invoicing & payments card boxes.
custom_expected:
The Create Role page opens with a Basic Details section and a permissions section.

The permissions are pre-filled to match the Service Advisor template (for example Work orders View and Create & Edit on, Delete off).

title: You can change any setting from the template defaults before saving
custom_preconds: 1. You started from the Service Advisor template on the Create Role page.
custom_steps:
1. On the Schedule card, untick Delete.
  2. Confirm Schedule View and Create & Edit stay ticked.
  3. In Page Access, turn Reports on.
  4. Type a Role name.
  5. Click Create.
  6. Afterwards open the role's Permission Summary.
custom_expected:
Delete unticks; Schedule View and Create & Edit stay ticked.

Reports turns on.

Create works.

The Permission Summary shows Schedule with View and Create & Edit only and Reports on.

title: A successful Create shows a success message and returns to the list
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Create Role page with a valid name and at least one permission.
custom_steps: 1. Click Create.
custom_expected: A success message 'Role created successfully.' appears, the app returns to the Roles & Permissions list, and the new role appears with type Custom and 0 users.

title: Same name and permissions as an existing role shows a 'Similar role already exists' confirmation
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Create Role page and a role with the same name and identical permissions already exists.
custom_steps:
1. Enter the same name and identical permissions as the existing role.
  2. Click Create.
custom_expected:
Instead of an error, a confirmation appears: 'Similar role already exists', explaining a role with identical permissions already exists, with Cancel and Create Anyway buttons.

Your entered name and selections are kept.

title: Turning on every permission shows the 'Full administrative access' warning banner
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Create Role page.
custom_steps:
1. Apply the Administrator template (which turns on every permission).
  2. Look at the banner.
custom_expected: A warning banner titled 'Full administrative access' appears, saying the role has every permission enabled and to make sure that is intended before saving.

title: A role name must be unique
custom_preconds: 1. A role named 'QA Unique Test Role' already exists.
custom_steps:
1. Start creating a role, pick any template and apply it.
  2. Type 'QA Unique Test Role' as the Role name.
  3. Click Create.
custom_expected: Saving is blocked because the name is already used.

title: The template picker may use shorter role names than the Roles list
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles list and open the template picker.
custom_steps:
1. Read the role names in the template picker.
  2. Close it.
  3. Read the role names in the Roles list.
  4. Compare them.
custom_expected:
The Roles list uses the full names (Administrator, Parts Technician, Office User, Time Clock User).

The template picker may show shorter names (for example Admin, Parts Tech, Office, Time Clock) — confirm the exact picker labels live and flag any that differ from the list.

title: The template picker descriptions differ from the Roles list descriptions
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles list and open the template picker.
custom_steps:
1. For each template, read the description under the name.
  2. Compare with the Description shown for the same role on the Roles list.
custom_expected:
Each template shows a short, action-oriented description.

These short descriptions differ from the fuller sentences in the Roles list Description column — they come from two different copy sources.

(Confirm the exact picker description text live.)

title: Edit opens the role editor pre-filled with the role's current settings
custom_preconds: 1. A custom role named 'QA Edit Target' exists with known settings (Work orders View + Create & Edit, Schedule View, Reports ON, See Financial Data OFF, everything else off).
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings > Roles & Permissions.
  2. Find the 'QA Edit Target' row.
  3. Click the pencil icon in the Actions column.
  4. Look at the page that opens.
  5. Look at the Role name and Description fields.
  6. Look at every card and toggle.
custom_expected:
The role editor opens.

Role name and Description are pre-filled with the role's current values.

Every setting matches the saved role: Work orders View on, Create & Edit on, Delete off; Schedule View on; Reports on; See Financial Data off; everything else off.

title: Saving an edited role shows 'Role updated successfully.' after a confirmation dialog
custom_preconds: 1. You are editing an existing custom role.
custom_steps:
1. Change one or more permissions.
  2. Click Save.
  3. Confirm in the dialog.
custom_expected:
A confirmation dialog appears listing the added and removed permissions, with a 'don't show this again' option and Cancel/Confirm buttons.

After confirming, a green success message 'Role updated successfully.' appears and you return to the roles list.

title: Reset to template restores template defaults; Save is only enabled if something changed
custom_preconds:
1. Log in as a user who can edit roles.
  2. At least one custom role (created from a template) exists.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings > Roles & Permissions.
  2. Open the custom role with the pencil (Edit) icon.
  3. Click Reset to template.
  4. Look at the Save button.
custom_expected:
If the role's permissions had been changed from the template defaults: Reset to template puts them back to the defaults and enables Save; clicking Save keeps the reset.

If the role still matched the template defaults: Reset to template changes nothing and Save stays disabled.

title: Changing a role logs an active user out; new permissions apply at next login
custom_preconds: 1. A test user 'Tester Bob' is assigned the role 'QA Edit Target' and is logged in in a second browser session.
custom_steps:
1. As Admin, go to Settings > Roles & Permissions and click the pencil on 'QA Edit Target'.
  2. In the Work orders card, untick View.
  3. Confirm Create & Edit and Delete also untick.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Switch to Bob's session and try to move around the app.
  6. Have Bob log back in.
  7. Look at Bob's top navigation.
custom_expected:
Create & Edit and Delete untick automatically.

Save works.

Bob is sent to the login page (or sees a session-ended message).

After logging back in, Work Orders is no longer in Bob's top navigation.

title: The Office User system role cannot be edited (lock icon, eye only)
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Find the Office User row.
  2. Look at the Actions column.
  3. Click the eye icon.
custom_expected:
There is no pencil icon; only the eye icon.

A read-only Permission Summary opens for Office User.

title: The Time Clock User system role cannot be edited (lock icon, eye only)
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Find the Time Clock User row.
  2. Look at the Actions column.
  3. Click the eye icon.
custom_expected:
There is no pencil icon; only the eye icon.

A read-only Permission Summary opens for Time Clock User.

title: The role name cannot be left empty when editing
custom_preconds: 1. You are editing an existing role.
custom_steps:
1. Clear the Role name field.
  2. Try to Save.
custom_expected:
A message 'Role name is a required field' appears under the 'Role name*' label.

Save is blocked; the role cannot be saved with an empty name.

title: Editing: at least one permission must be turned on to save
custom_preconds: 1. You are editing an editable role.
custom_steps:
1. Untick every box in every card.
  2. Turn off every Page Access toggle, Settings sub-toggle, Parts Department card and Cross-Cutting Toggle.
  3. Click Save.
custom_expected: Save is blocked and a message tells you at least one permission must be turned on.

title: A custom role with 0 users can be deleted from the three-dot menu
custom_preconds: 1. A custom role named 'QA Delete OK' exists and its Users count is 0.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings > Roles & Permissions.
  2. Find the 'QA Delete OK' row.
  3. Click the three-dot menu in the Actions column.
  4. Click Delete.
  5. Look at the confirmation dialog.
  6. Confirm the delete.
  7. Look at the list and any message.
custom_expected:
The three-dot menu shows a Delete option.

A confirmation dialog appears.

After confirming, the 'QA Delete OK' row is gone from the list.

title: A custom role with 1 or more users cannot be deleted
custom_preconds: 1. A custom role is assigned to at least 1 user.
custom_steps:
1. Try to delete the role from the list three-dot menu.
  2. Open the role editor and look at the Delete role control.
custom_expected:
Deletion is prevented in two ways: (1) the list three-dot menu hides the Delete option when the role has users (it shows only View Permissions); (2) in the editor the Delete role button is disabled, with the tooltip 'This role is assigned to 1 user(s). Reassign them to another role before deleting.'

Note: there is no separate 'Cannot Delete' pop-up — the block is the hidden menu item plus the disabled button and tooltip.

title: After moving the assigned users to another role, the role can be deleted
custom_preconds: 1. A custom role 'QA Delete Blocked' has exactly 1 user assigned.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings > Staff and find the user assigned to 'QA Delete Blocked'.
  2. Open the user's role dropdown.
  3. Change the user's role to a different one (for example Technician).
  4. Save.
  5. Go back to Settings > Roles & Permissions.
  6. Check the Users count on 'QA Delete Blocked' now reads 0.
  7. Open the three-dot menu, click Delete and confirm.
custom_expected:
The reassignment works.

The Users count shows 0.

A confirmation dialog appears; after confirming, the role is deleted.

title: System roles have no Delete option anywhere
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. For each of the 11 system roles, look at the Actions column.
  2. For the editable system roles that have a three-dot menu (for example Service Manager, Foreman), open the menu.
  3. Look at the menu options.
custom_expected:
Administrator, Office User and Time Clock User show only the eye icon (no three-dot menu).

The other editable system roles show a pencil, an eye and a three-dot menu.

None of the three-dot menus has a Delete option.

title: The assigned-user count is correct when a delete is blocked
custom_preconds: 1. A custom role is assigned to exactly one user.
custom_steps:
1. Reach the delete-blocked state for that role.
  2. Read the user count shown.
custom_expected: The count shown is 1, matching the one assigned user.

title: The eye icon on the Roles list opens the read-only Permission Summary
custom_preconds:
1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
  2. The Senior Service Advisor row is visible.
custom_steps:
1. Find the Senior Service Advisor row.
  2. Click the eye icon in the Actions column.
  3. Look at the window that opens.
  4. Scroll through every part of it.
  5. Try to click any checkbox or toggle inside it.
  6. Close the window.
custom_expected:
A window opens.

It shows the add/edit/delete areas, the Page Access toggles, the Settings sub-toggles, the Work orders sub-settings (View mode, Review work orders, Pick parts, Order parts), and the Cross-Cutting Toggles (See Financial Data, View and Manage AP/AR Data) for Senior Service Advisor.

Everything in the window is read-only; clicking does nothing.

The window closes when you close it.

title: You can view a role's Permission Summary from Edit Staff Member using the eye icon next to the Role dropdown
custom_preconds:
1. Log in as a user who can edit staff (for example an Administrator).
  2. At least one staff member exists.
custom_steps:
1. Go to the Staff page (Settings > Staff).
  2. Open a staff member to bring up the Edit Staff Member window.
  3. Find the Role dropdown and the eye icon next to it.
  4. Click the eye icon.
custom_expected:
There is an eye icon next to the Role dropdown on the Edit Staff Member window.

Clicking it opens a read-only Permission Summary for the role currently chosen in the dropdown.

The summary lists that role's permissions with no way to edit them.

title: The eye icon on the Office row opens the Permission Summary
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Find the Office User row.
  2. Click the eye icon (the only icon in the Actions column for this row).
custom_expected: A read-only Permission Summary opens for Office User.

title: The eye icon on the Time Clock User row opens the Permission Summary
custom_preconds: 1. You are on the Roles & Permissions list.
custom_steps:
1. Find the Time Clock User row.
  2. Click the eye icon.
custom_expected: A read-only Permission Summary opens for Time Clock User.

title: The Permission Summary is grouped and shows each setting's on/off state
custom_preconds: 1. A Permission Summary is open for Service Manager.
custom_steps:
1. Scroll through the window.
  2. For the add/edit/delete areas, check how the state is shown.
  3. For the toggles, check how the state is shown.
  4. For View mode, check how the value is shown.
custom_expected:
Every setting is clearly labelled with its on/off state.

The content is grouped into the add/edit/delete areas, the Page Access toggles, the Settings sub-toggles, the Work orders sub-settings (View mode, Review work orders, Pick parts, Order parts), and the Cross-Cutting Toggles (See Financial Data, View and Manage AP/AR Data, View History Logs).

title: Work orders View gives access to the work order list and detail
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders View only (no Create & Edit, no Delete).
custom_steps:
1. Log in as that user and look at the top navigation.
  2. Click Work Orders.
  3. Open a work order by clicking a row.
  4. Look for any create, edit or delete options.
custom_expected:
Work Orders is in the top navigation.

The work order list opens.

The work order detail opens.

There is no New work order/Create button; fields are read-only; there is no delete option.

title: Work orders Create & Edit lets the user create and change work orders
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders View and Create & Edit (no Delete).
custom_steps:
1. Log in and open Work Orders.
  2. Click the create-new button.
  3. Fill the required fields (customer, asset).
  4. Save.
  5. Open the saved work order and change the status, lead technician and service advisor.
  6. Save.
  7. Look for a delete option.
custom_expected:
The Create button is shown.

The new work order is created.

The edits are saved.

There is no delete option.

title: Work orders Delete lets the user delete work orders
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders View, Create & Edit and Delete.
custom_steps:
1. Log in and open a non-critical work order.
  2. Click the Delete action.
  3. Confirm.
  4. Return to the list.
custom_expected:
The Delete action is shown.

A confirmation dialog appears.

The deleted work order is gone from the list.

title: Work orders View OFF hides Work Orders from the top navigation
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders View OFF.
custom_steps: 1. Log in and look at the top navigation.
custom_expected: Work Orders is not in the top navigation (other items the user has access to still show).

title: The Work orders sub-toggles are shown but disabled when Work orders View is OFF
custom_preconds: 1. Open Create Role (or edit a custom role) with Work orders View OFF.
custom_steps:
1. Find the Work orders card.
  2. Find the three sub-toggles Review work orders, Pick parts and Order parts.
  3. Look at their state.
  4. Try to click each one.
custom_expected:
All three sub-toggles are shown inside the Work orders card but appear greyed out / disabled.

Clicking them does not turn them on.

title: The Review work orders sub-toggle controls the Review action on work orders
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders View and Create & Edit, View mode Full View, and Review work orders ON.
custom_steps:
1. Log in and open a work order where Review applies.
  2. Look for a Review action.
  3. As an admin, edit the role and turn Review work orders OFF, then save.
  4. Have the user log back in and reopen the work order.
  5. Look for the Review action again.
custom_expected:
The Review action is shown and works when Review work orders is on.

After turning it off, the Review action is no longer shown.

title: Pick parts needs only Work orders View, not Create & Edit
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders View only (Create & Edit and Delete OFF), Pick parts ON and the Parts Department card ON.
custom_steps:
1. Log in and open a work order.
  2. Find a Pick parts action.
  3. Pick parts from inventory onto a line.
  4. Save.
  5. Move a part from one line to another on the same work order.
  6. Move a part between two different work orders.
custom_expected:
The Pick parts action is available even without Create & Edit on Work orders.

The pick and the moves all work.

title: Order parts needs Work orders View and See Financial Data (not Create & Edit)
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders View ON (Create & Edit OFF), See Financial Data ON, Order parts ON and the Parts Department card ON.
custom_steps:
1. Log in and open a work order.
  2. Find the Order parts action.
  3. Start placing a purchase order for parts.
  4. Save the purchase order.
  5. Later, receive a parts delivery against the purchase order.
custom_expected:
The Order parts action is available even without Create & Edit on Work orders (Order parts needs only Work orders View plus See Financial Data).

Placing and receiving the order work.

If See Financial Data were off, turning on Order parts would prompt to enable See Financial Data first.

title: Pick parts and Order parts are independent toggles
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders View, Pick parts ON and Order parts OFF.
custom_steps:
1. Log in and open a work order.
  2. Try Pick parts.
  3. Try Order parts.
custom_expected:
Pick parts is available and works.

Order parts is hidden or disabled.

title: Without Create & Edit, create/edit options are hidden on work orders
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders View only.
custom_steps:
1. Log in and open the work order list.
  2. Look for any New work order/Create button.
  3. Open a work order and try to edit a header field.
custom_expected:
There is no create button.

The work order header fields are read-only.

title: Without Delete, no delete option is shown on a work order
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders View and Create & Edit (no Delete).
custom_steps:
1. Log in and open a work order.
  2. Look for any delete option (toolbar, three-dot menu, and so on).
custom_expected: There is no delete option anywhere on the work order detail.

title: Creating a work order still works when Customers View is OFF
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders View and Create & Edit ON and Customers View OFF.
custom_steps:
1. Log in and look at the top navigation.
  2. Open Work Orders and click the create-new button.
  3. Open the Customer selector in the new work order form.
  4. Search for or scroll to a customer.
  5. Select the customer.
  6. Fill the rest and save.
custom_expected:
Customers is not in the top navigation.

The customer selector inside the work order form still opens and lists customers (the data is reachable because it is needed to create a work order).

The customer can be selected and the work order saves.

title: The customer name shows on the work order header even when Customers View is OFF
custom_preconds:
1. A user has a role with Work orders View ON and Customers View OFF.
  2. An existing work order is for a known customer.
custom_steps:
1. Log in and confirm Customers is not in the top navigation.
  2. Open Work Orders and open the work order.
  3. Look at the work order header for the customer name.
  4. Try clicking the customer name if it looks like a link.
custom_expected:
Customers is hidden.

The customer name shows on the work order header (it is part of the work order record).

title: The 'Add Customer' button in the New Work Order flow when Customers Create & Edit is OFF
custom_preconds: 1. A user has a role with Work orders Create & Edit ON, Customers View ON and Customers Create & Edit OFF.
custom_steps:

  3. Look for an Add Customer button in the customer picker.

  4. Look for an Add Asset button in the asset picker.
custom_expected:

Adding an asset here is part of creating a work order (Work Orders: Create & Edit). It does NOT require Customers: Create & Edit.

  5. Log back in as that user and open a work order.
  6. Look for the Parts tab.
custom_expected:
With Order parts on, the work order Parts tab is shown and can be opened.

With Order parts off, the Parts tab is hidden.

The Parts tab visibility is controlled by Order parts.

title: Return part & resolve cores allowed with Work Orders: View
refs: SV-8541 (Custom Roles & Permissions "Marking Cores OK/Not Ok is gated by WO→View"; parent SV-8183 §9 WO/Parts enforcement mapping)

title: PARTS_DEPARTMENT is a UI-only gate - not exercisable as a server-side fePermission cascade (out of scope)
custom_preconds: Authenticated.

2. POST /api/roles with fe_permissions=['partSalesView'] and cross_toggles.seeFinancialData=true (PARTS_DEPARTMENT cannot be sent - it is not a settable fePermission).

custom_steps:
1. Click Parts, open Returns, and open a return record.
2. Click Delete and confirm.
custom_expected: The return is deleted and removed from the Returns list.

title: Verify Senior Service Advisor can reverse a work order invoice
custom_preconds:
Log in to ShopView as a user assigned the Senior Service Advisor role. (reversing a work order invoice requires Work Orders: Delete per spec v33; this role has it).
The work order already has an invoice created on its Finance tab.
Note: an OVER LIMIT badge on the customer does not block reversing an invoice.
custom_steps:
1. Open the work order's Finance tab.
2. Click Reverse on the invoice and confirm.
custom_expected: The invoice is reversed successfully.

title: Verify Senior Service Advisor can reverse a Part Sales invoice
custom_preconds:
Log in to ShopView as a user assigned the Senior Service Advisor role. (reversing a Part Sales invoice requires Part Sales: Delete per spec v33; this role has it).
At least one Part Sales invoice exists under Part Sales.
custom_steps:
1. Click Part Sales and open an existing invoice.
2. Click Reverse and confirm.
custom_expected: The Part Sales invoice is reversed successfully.

title: Verify Senior Service Advisor can edit and delete another user's work order note
custom_preconds:
1. Log in as a user with the Senior Service Advisor role.
2. The role has Work Orders > View turned ON.
3. The role has Work Orders > Delete turned ON.
4. A work order exists that already has a note written by a DIFFERENT user (e.g., an Admin).
custom_steps:
1. Open the work order.
2. Click the Notes tab.
3. Find the note written by the other user.
4. Click the note's menu and choose Edit.
5. Change the text and click Save.
6. Open the note's menu again and choose Delete.
7. Confirm the deletion.
custom_expected:
1. The Edit option is available on the other user's note (Work Orders > View allows editing ANY note for team collaboration).
2. The edited text saves successfully with no permission error.
3. The Delete option is also available on the other user's note (Work Orders > Delete allows deleting ANY note, including other users').
4. The other user's note is deleted with no permission error.

title: Verify Service Advisor can see all pricing and financial data on a work order

Note: the role may display as 'Junior Service Advisor' in the build (the spec calls it 'Service Advisor').
At least one work order exists that contains labor and part lines with prices entered.
custom_steps:
1. Click Work Orders and open a work order.
  2. Check line prices and totals.
  3. Open the Finance card and the Stats tab.
custom_expected: All money values (line prices, totals, Finance card, Stats tab) are visible with actual amounts.

title: Verify Service Advisor cannot delete a work order
custom_preconds:
Log in to ShopView as a user assigned the Service Advisor role. (this role has Work Orders = View/Create and Edit, NO Delete).
Note: the role may display as 'Junior Service Advisor' in the build (the spec calls it 'Service Advisor').
The work order is in Uncomplete status (a work order must be Uncomplete before it can be deleted).
custom_steps:
1. Open the Uncomplete work order.
2. Open the work order action menu and look for a Delete option; if present, click it.
custom_expected: Deleting the work order is BLOCKED even though the work order is Uncomplete: the Delete action is hidden or disabled, or clicking it returns a permission error.

title: Verify Service Advisor can create an invoice on a work order

At least one work order exists.

1. Open the work order and go to the Finance tab.
2. Click Create Invoice, complete the dialog, and save.
custom_expected: The invoice is created successfully and appears on the Finance tab.

title: Verify Service Advisor is blocked from deleting a payment while Manage AP/AR is OFF
custom_preconds:
Log in to ShopView as a user assigned the Service Advisor role. (this role has Invoicing and Payments: Delete, but Manage Accounts Payable and Receivable is OFF; per spec v33 / SV-7913, Invoicing Delete additionally requires Manage AP/AR ON - this blocking is intended, not a bug).
Note: the role may display as 'Junior Service Advisor' in the build (the spec calls it 'Service Advisor').
The work order already has an invoice created on its Finance tab.
A payment has been recorded against the invoice.
custom_steps:
1. Open the work order's Finance tab and locate the payment.
2. Try to delete the payment.
custom_expected: Deleting the payment is BLOCKED (a configuration prompt or permission block appears) because Manage AP/AR is OFF, even though the role has Invoicing Delete. This is the intended behavior per SV-7913.

custom_preconds: WO V \u2713 | Invoicing V \u2713 | See Financial \u2713 | (no Invoicing Edit) | View Mode: Full (View Mode as specified).
custom_steps:
1. Configure a custom role per the Setup in Preconditions; assign to a test user and log in.
  2. Open the Finance tab; look for create-invoice / take-payment / deposit controls.
custom_expected:
Can view invoices + the Finance tab (§1h View). Cannot create invoices / process payments / collect deposits / send to terminal (all Edit). Those controls hidden or disabled.

Risk / Rationale: Create/payment actions exposed with Invoicing View only.
Spec Ref: §1h Invoicing View vs Edit

title: CR-BRK-024 — Financial Data Confirmation Modal — Cancel path
custom_preconds: See Financial \u2717 → enable a Part Sales or Invoicing checkbox → modal appears → Cancel (View Mode as specified).
custom_steps:
1. Configure a custom role per the Setup in Preconditions; assign to a test user and log in.
  2. Trigger the modal by checking Part Sales/Invoicing while See Financial OFF; click Cancel.
custom_expected:
Cancel reverts the checkbox to its previous state; See Financial stays OFF; the Part Sales/Invoicing checkbox is unchecked (Financial Data Confirmation Modal).

Risk / Rationale: Cancel leaves the checkbox checked, or turns See Financial ON anyway.
Spec Ref: Financial Data Confirmation Modal

title: CR-BRK-026 — Admin role edited to remove Admin pages — self-lockout protection
custom_preconds: Edit the Admin system role; attempt to turn OFF App Settings (houses Roles & Permissions) (View Mode as specified).
custom_steps:
1. Configure a custom role per the Setup in Preconditions; assign to a test user and log in.
  2. Open Admin in the editor; attempt to disable App Settings; save.
custom_expected:
Admin cannot be edited to lose access to the Admin pages (Open Q9: 'Admin system role cannot be edited to lose access to the Admin pages'). The toggle should be prevented/locked.

Risk / Rationale: Admin can remove its own Admin-page access → self-lockout risk.
Spec Ref: Open Q9; Roles list

title: CR-BRK-027 — Office / Time Clock edit attempt — non-editable roles
custom_preconds: In Roles list: click Office; click Time Clock (View Mode as specified).
custom_steps:
1. Configure a custom role per the Setup in Preconditions; assign to a test user and log in.
  2. Click Office and Time Clock in the Roles list.
custom_expected:
Office and Time Clock cannot be edited — clicking opens a read-only permission summary (Concepts + Roles list).

Risk / Rationale: The editor opens (editable) instead of the read-only summary.
Spec Ref: Roles & Permissions List; Concepts

title: CR-BRK-028 — Delete role with users assigned — guard
custom_preconds: A custom role with 1+ users assigned; attempt to delete it (View Mode as specified).
custom_steps:
1. Configure a custom role per the Setup in Preconditions; assign to a test user and log in.
  2. Attempt to delete a role that has assigned users.
custom_expected:
'Cannot Delete' modal appears; the confirm/delete button is disabled until all users are reassigned (Delete Role).

Risk / Rationale: Deletion proceeds and orphans the assigned users.
Spec Ref: Delete Role

title: CR-BRK-029 — Role change — forced logout / stale permissions
custom_preconds: Change an active (logged-in) user's role (View Mode as specified).
custom_steps:
1. Configure a custom role per the Setup in Preconditions; assign to a test user and log in.
  2. Change a logged-in user's role; observe forced logout and new perms on re-login.
custom_expected:
The affected user is forced to log out; the new role applies on next login (Staff Page + Key Decision 'Role change = forced logout').

Risk / Rationale: User keeps the old session/permissions until a manual logout — stale permissions persist.
Spec Ref: Staff Page Updates; Key Decisions

title: CR-BRK-030 — Timesheets OFF but Reports ON — surface exposure
custom_preconds: WO V \u2713 | Timesheets \u2717 | Reports \u2713 | View Mode: Full (View Mode as specified).
custom_steps:
1. Configure a custom role per the Setup in Preconditions; assign to a test user and log in.
  2. Confirm Timesheets nav hidden; open Reports → timesheet activities report (should be visible).
custom_expected:
Timesheets nav hidden, BUT the timesheet activities report is still visible via Reports (§1i View note). Clock in/out remains available to all.

Risk / Rationale: Either the report is wrongly hidden, or timesheet-editing surfaces leak beyond the read-only report.
Spec Ref: §1i Timesheets; §2a Reports

title: Custom role (WO Lines C&E on, Delete off): delete/reopen inspections on a Completed line respects the atom, not line status
custom_preconds:
Digital Inspections feature enabled on the org.
Custom role: Work Orders View + Create & Edit + Delete; Work Order Lines Create & Edit ON, Delete OFF; View Mode Full View.
A user assigned to that custom role.
A work order in an editable status with one line carrying three inspections in different statuses (in progress, not started, completed), then the parent WO line driven to Complete while the WO stays editable.

custom_steps_separated.content: Log in as the custom-role user and open the work order; expand the Completed line.
custom_steps_separated.expected: All inspection sub-rows render (Open visible) even though the line is Complete.

custom_steps_separated.content: Attempt to delete an incomplete (in-progress / not-started) inspection on the Completed line.
custom_steps_separated.expected: Allowed — the remove (bin) affordance is present and the inspection is deleted. Create & Edit covers deleting an incomplete inspection regardless of the line's Complete status.

custom_steps_separated.content: Attempt to delete a completed inspection on the Completed line.
custom_steps_separated.expected: Not allowed — the remove (bin) affordance is absent for the completed inspection because the role lacks WO Lines: Delete.

custom_steps_separated.content: Open the completed inspection's locked view and attempt to reopen it.
custom_steps_separated.expected: Not allowed — the Reopen button is hidden because the role lacks WO Lines: Delete.

title: Administrator - A. View inspections on a work order line
custom_preconds: Logged in as Administrator. A work order line has at least one inspection.
custom_steps:
1. Log in.
  2. Open a work order that has an inspection on a line.
  3. Locate the inspection on the line.
custom_expected:
Step 1: Login succeeds.
Step 2: Work order opens.
Step 3: Existing inspections on the line are visible. Edit controls appear only if the role has the relevant WOL rights; otherwise read-only. (SV-8095: View = Work Orders: View.)

title: Administrator - B. Add inspection to a work order line
custom_preconds: Logged in as Administrator. A work order with at least one line exists.
custom_steps:
1. Log in.
  2. Open a work order and locate a line.
  3. Open the three-dot menu on the line.
  4. Select Add Inspection and choose a template.
custom_expected:
Step 3: The three-dot menu shows Add Inspection.
Step 4: The inspection template is added and "Inspection added to line." is shown. (Gated by WOL Create and Edit - SV-8095 AC2.)

title: Administrator - C. Add multiple inspection templates to one line
custom_preconds: Logged in as Administrator. A work order line exists.
custom_steps:
1. Log in.
  2. Add an inspection template to a line.
  3. Add a second and third template to the same line.
  4. Attempt to add a fourth.
custom_expected:
Step 2: First inspection added ("Inspection added to line.").
Step 3: Second and third inspections added to the same line.
Step 4: VIU - spec does not state a maximum; build observed up to 3 per line. Confirm whether a 4th is prevented.

title: Administrator - D. Open and fill an in-progress inspection
custom_preconds: Logged in as Administrator. A line has an in-progress inspection (incl. on an approved line for Tech View roles).
custom_steps:
1. Log in.
  2. Open an in-progress inspection on a line (click Open).
  3. Attempt to fill/edit the inspection items.
custom_expected:
Step 2: The inspection opens.
Step 3: Inspection items can be filled/edited. (WOL Create and Edit - SV-8095 AC2.)

title: Administrator - E. Complete an inspection (Submit and Generate Report)
custom_preconds: Logged in as Administrator. An inspection is in progress with required fields fillable.
custom_steps:
1. Log in.
  2. Open an in-progress inspection.
  3. Fill all required fields.
  4. Click Submit and Generate Report.
custom_expected:
Step 3: With no required field outstanding, Submit and Generate Report is visible and clickable.
Step 4: The inspection is submitted, a report is generated, status becomes "Completed".

title: Administrator - F. Inspection at 100 percent but not submitted shows Open
custom_preconds: Logged in as Administrator. An inspection can be filled to 100 percent without submitting.
custom_steps:
1. Log in.
  2. Fill all inspection items to 100 percent but do NOT click Submit and Generate Report.
  3. Observe the inspection status on the line.
custom_expected:
Step 2: All items show filled (100 percent).
Step 3: The inspection still shows "Open" (not "Completed") until Submit and Generate Report is clicked.

title: Administrator - G. Inspection status labels display correctly
custom_preconds: Logged in as Administrator. A line has inspections in different states.
custom_steps:
1. Open a work order line with inspections in different states.
  2. Observe the status labels.
custom_expected: Step 2: A completed inspection shows "Completed"; an in-progress inspection shows "In Progress" with a percentage of completion.

title: Administrator - H. Remove an incomplete (in-progress) inspection
custom_preconds: Logged in as Administrator. A line has an in-progress / not-started (incomplete) inspection.
custom_steps:
1. Log in.
  2. Open the line with an incomplete inspection.
  3. Look for / click the bin (remove) icon.
  4. Confirm removal if prompted.
custom_expected:
Step 3: A confirmation dialog appears: "Remove inspection - Are you sure you want to remove this inspection?" (Cancel / Remove).
Step 4: On Remove, the incomplete inspection is removed. (Removing an INCOMPLETE inspection is gated by WOL Create and Edit - SV-8095 AC3A, finalized.)

title: Administrator - I. Remove a completed inspection
custom_preconds: Logged in as Administrator. A line has a completed inspection with a generated PDF report.
custom_steps:
1. Log in.
  2. Open the line with a completed inspection.
  3. Look for / click the bin (remove) icon.
  4. Confirm removal if prompted.
custom_expected:
Step 3: A confirmation dialog appears: "Remove inspection - This inspection has a generated PDF report. Are you sure you want to remove it?" (Cancel / Remove).
Step 4: On Remove, the completed inspection is removed. (Deleting a COMPLETED inspection is gated by WOL Delete - SV-8095 AC3B, finalized.)
Build note: removal may require the WO line to NOT be marked complete (mark line Uncomplete first).

title: Administrator - J. Reopen a completed inspection
custom_preconds: Logged in as Administrator. A line has a completed inspection.
custom_steps:
1. Log in.
  2. Open the line with a completed inspection.

custom_expected:

Note: confirm the reopen MECHANIC for an inspection already submitted with a generated PDF (the permission is settled = WOL Delete; only the mechanic needs a UI check).
